produced_by: the adapter-test invocation recorded below, run against oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/
purpose: The structured run record of the adapter-test invocation: its exact command, its interpreter's path and version, a per-test-module outcome, a separate outcome entry for every negative fixture, and the exit status. AAP 0.6.1 gives this file its row. It is the evidence that the normalizer is CORRECT rather than merely FINISHED -- every claim of adapter correctness in oss-scan-results/ rests on the results enumerated here.
publication: harness/artifacts/** is git-ignored (.gitignore:31 is artifacts/), so this record is published through the per-file size-and-sha256 manifest that oss-scan-results/run-record.md owns, rather than through ordinary git collection.
why_a_per_fixture_enumeration_rather_tha: AAP 0.6.2 requires a negative fixture for every rejection condition each exercised adapter can produce, whether or not this run's own artifacts contained that case, because "a rejection path with no test is a rejection path nobody has exercised". A single aggregate pass count would satisfy a CI system and tell a reader nothing about whether the rejection paths were ever exercised. So negative_fixtures below carries one entry per fixture, naming the fixture file, the adapter, the rejection class asserted and the expected count.

governing_rules.read_completeness: review_rules was called with view_range [1, -1] and returned exactly that one line. That is a COMPLETE read, not a truncated one: no rules document exists.
corroboration: AAP 0.7 -- "No user-specified rules were provided for this project; enterprise-standard best practice applies in their place"
governing_rules.consequence: No rule forces anything into this file's scope and inventing one would be fabrication. The absence is expressly NOT licence to lower the bar, so the substitute standard below is applied in full.
governing_rules.note: Every one of the eight test modules states the same finding independently in its own module docstring.

substitute_standard.basis: AAP's four principles, applied in place of absent user rules.

how_this_run_honours_it: the positive fixtures are unmodified captured excerpts of real tool output, so an adapter is tested against the shape the tool emits rather than the shape someone believed it emits (AAP 0.6.2)
the expected results are hand-verified and asserted field by field, never generated by running the adapter under test

the per-fixture outcomes below come from a collector that drove the committed suite unmodified through unittest's own API and recorded what actually executed -- it added no assertion of its own and asserted nothing about the adapters

the reconciliation identity's left-hand side comes from normalize.reconcile.count_records, a traversal that builds no row, and test_reconciliation asserts that independence structurally against the import graph rather than by observing agreement on a fixture

2_reject_rather_than_infer.requirement: Every rejection condition an adapter can produce has a negative fixture and assertion, whether or not this run's artifacts contained that case.
2_reject_rather_than_infer.how_this_run_honours_it: 38 negative fixtures are committed and every one was exercised by executed, passing assertions. rejection_condition_coverage below cross-checks that set against the nine conditions AAP 0.5.4 enumerates and names, per adapter, which conditions that adapter can and cannot produce.

3_halt_and_report_over_silent_repair.requirement: AAP 0.8.1; AAP 0.9.2 makes a failed adapter fixture, rejection or reconciliation test a condition that STOPS THE RUN.
3_halt_and_report_over_silent_repair.how_this_run_honours_it: exit_status below carries halt semantics explicitly: a failure would have been recorded as a halt, never as a soft warning. No assertion was weakened, skipped, or expected-failed to obtain a green result -- skipped, expectedFailures and unexpectedSuccesses are all zero and are reported rather than omitted.

never_fabricate_a_measurement.rule: A recorded pass for a test that did not run is the worst outcome available to this file.
how_it_is_enforced_here: every module entry's tests_run, elapsed and exit status come from that module's own individual invocation, not from the whole-suite total divided up
the per-module counts sum to exactly the whole-suite count (98+100+81+75+74+62+47+40 = 577), so neither figure is a restatement of the other

every negative-fixture entry carries observed attribution -- the number of executed subTests that named that fixture and their outcomes -- alongside the expected counts, so a fixture that was committed but never reached would show zero naming subtests instead of an unearned pass

corrections_recorded_rather_than_quietly: an earlier inspection of this tree miscounted it as 54 expected files and 37 negative fixtures. The measured, git-tracked counts are 52 and 38 (git ls-files agrees for both directories) and the corrected figures are the ones used throughout this record.

the first invocation attempted added -t . to the documented command form and unittest raised "ImportError: Start directory is not importable" with exit 1, because oss-scan-results/adapter-tests is not an importable package. That was an invocation error on the caller's part and NOT a test outcome; the documented form, which passes -s without -t, runs clean. It is recorded here so the exit 1 cannot later be mistaken for a suite failure.

command.third_party_test_runner_note: pytest 9.1.1 happens to be importable on this host and was deliberately NOT used: every test module imports unittest and none imports pytest, so the suite needs no plugin and no install step (AAP 0.4.1, AAP 0.4.3).
command.command_form_authority: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/test_shape_routing_negative.py lines 44-51, which names this file: "That exact command is what harness/artifacts/logs/adapter-tests-run.json records and oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/README.md echoes." Every one of the eight modules documents the same discover form.
command.no_t_flag: The documented form passes -s and no -t. Adding -t . makes discovery treat the start directory as an importable package, which it is not, and unittest exits 1 with ImportError before running a single test. The modules do not need it: each performs a one-time sys.path insertion of <repo>/harness/lib derived from __file__, so the suite imports the normalize package identically from any working directory.

per_module_commands.purpose: Each module was ALSO run on its own, so its tests_run and exit status below are its own measurement rather than a share of the aggregate.

environment.note: The suite needs none of these variables -- it derives every path from __file__ -- but the environment was sourced and verified so this invocation ran under the same environment as the rest of the run.

interpreter.independent_of_every_scanner_environment: The tests import only the standard library, so they run on the base interpreter and touch neither /opt/blitzy-tools/venvs/semgrep nor /opt/blitzy-tools/venvs/checkov (AAP 0.4.1). Semgrep and Checkov have separate virtualenvs by necessity -- conflicting dependencies -- and nothing here depends on either.

interpreter.difference_disposition: A difference of any kind is recorded with both values and the run continues (AAP 0.9.3). A patch-level difference is not a halt; only a JVM major-version misassignment halts, and no JVM is involved in this invocation.

entries.aap_condition: a record that cannot be attributed to a section

A fallback to Secret or Match would carry a matched secret value into the dataset, so the absence must reject rather than substitute -- and the structural sweeps assert no secret value reaches any field of any row OR of any rejection.

entries.aap_condition: a start_line present but not an integer

entries.continuation_proof: the traversal is asserted to continue past each rejected record, so a malformed element cannot silently truncate the remainder of the array

entries.user_example_guarded: This is where the user's worked leading-slash example is enforced: file_path is scan-root-relative DESPITE its leading slash, and reading it as filesystem-absolute would produce a long ../ chain and a silently false in_scope. The resolution is reconciled against the record's own file_abs_path, and an unreconcilable record rejects under a named class rather than resolving to a plausible wrong path.

entries.aap_condition: a start_line present but not an integer (and, in the same fixture, three malformed records)
entries.mixed_class_note: The only negative fixture in the tree asserting two DIFFERENT classes from one document. It is the strongest case against a test that merely counts rejections: four rejections would pass a count-only assertion under any class allocation, and only the per-class breakdown distinguishes a non-integer file_line_range[0] from a structurally broken record.

entries.both_shapes: every negative condition is asserted to behave identically in Checkov's array form as in its object form, so a rejection path cannot exist in one shape and be missing from the other

entries.path_convention: this tool's filePath is filesystem-ABSOLUTE, so the ordinary route is relativization to the SPARK_SRC root; the fixture's defective dependency has no usable filePath and both of its vulnerabilities reject

entries.field_coupling: rule_id and cve both derive from the vulnerability's name, so the fixture pins that an absent name rejects rather than producing a row with both fields absent

entries.aap_condition: a dependency-oriented record for which no package coordinate can be formed
entries.precedence_context: the four-level candidate precedence is asserted level by level elsewhere in the module; this fixture is the case where every level is exhausted, and it asserts a counted rejection rather than a row with a null package_coordinate
entries.why_realistic: Dependency-Check's in-scope surface here is vendored JS and CSS bundles, which routinely carry no resolvable coordinate at all.

entries.why_native_to_this_adapter: the artifact's own file field is an ephemeral /tmp/jimple2cpg-<id>/... path for every finding, so the path must be resolved from the class coordinate; a class that resolves to nothing under either source tree is a counted rejection, and any collector explanation for the unmappable coordinate is retained in the rejection record rather than in a dataset field

entries.condition_is_unique_to_this_adapter: Joern is the only tool whose row requires resolving a bytecode class coordinate against the filesystem, so it is the only adapter that can produce this class.
entries.asserted_twice: positively, that exactly three rejections arrive under the class named against paths.REJECT_CLASSES; and negatively, that NO colliding candidate reaches any field of any row -- the half a first-writer-wins implementation fails while every count still adds up.
entries.boundary_kept_sharp: an AMBIGUOUS coordinate is a rejection; a coordinate that resolves UNIQUELY into somewhere unwanted is a kept row with in_scope false. A fixture asserting only the first would accept "reject the inconvenient" as though it were "reject the ambiguous".

rejection_condition_coverage.requirement: AAP 0.9.4 -- a negative fixture and assertion for every rejection condition each EXERCISED adapter can produce, whether or not this run's own artifacts contained that case.
rejection_condition_coverage.cross_check_performed: The 38 committed negative fixtures were cross-checked against the nine conditions AAP 0.5.4 enumerates, per adapter, and each adapter's own declaration of which classes it can and cannot produce was read from the module rather than assumed.

nine_conditions_to_ten_classes.explanation: AAP 0.5.4 enumerates NINE conditions; normalize.paths.REJECT_CLASSES holds TEN members. The relationship is not a discrepancy: one condition splits into two classes, and one condition spans two.
nine_conditions_to_ten_classes.condition_1_splits: "an unresolvable or absent path" is realised as two classes -- absent_path where the record names no location at all, unresolvable_path where it names one that cannot be resolved. Keeping them apart is what lets a status document tell a defective producer from a defective base.
nine_conditions_to_ten_classes.condition_2_spans: "a cyclic, over-deep or invalid uriBaseId chain" spans unresolvable_path (the cycle, the over-depth, a base absent from the map with no fallback available, and a chain with no absolute ancestor) and invalid_uri (a syntactically invalid URI, which keeps its own class).
nine_conditions_to_ten_classes.arithmetic: 9 conditions -> 10 classes, with every one of the ten appearing in at least one asserted expectation.

rejection_condition_coverage.vocabulary_source: normalize.paths.REJECT_CLASSES, read from the module; no test retypes the list, so a class counted under a name no status document knows about cannot pass

unreachable_with_stated_reasons.unformable_package_coordinate: a Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, so package_coordinate is absent by design on every row and that absence is explicitly not a rejection
unreachable_with_stated_reasons.unattributable_section: this shape has no finding sections; scanner_class is fixed at sast for the whole artifact by AAP 0.5.4's class table

joern.sole_owner_of: ambiguous_source_resolution -- no other adapter resolves a bytecode coordinate against the filesystem, so no other adapter can produce it

rejection_condition_coverage.conclusion: Every condition every exercised adapter can produce is covered, by a committed negative fixture where the condition is a property of a record and by a named assertion where it is a property of the recorded invocation or of a record naming no location at all. Every class an adapter CANNOT produce is named with the reason, and in five of the six adapters that impossibility is itself asserted rather than merely described -- so a future change that made an unreachable class reachable would fail a test instead of passing unnoticed.
rejection_condition_coverage.unexercised_paths: none for the six adapters that exist. The one class no fixture in the tree claims is absent_path for Trivy, which that module names explicitly as not exercised and not claimed, with its reason. No adapter exists for osv-scanner, so it has no rejection paths to exercise.

shape_routing_negative.direction_asserted: a NATIVE artifact must NOT route to the SARIF adapter
shape_routing_negative.why_that_direction: "a permissive detector that accepts a native file as SARIF produces an empty result set rather than an error, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan" (AAP 0.5.4). findings.json is row-only, so a tool contributing no row is invisible in it by construction -- the detector is the only place the difference can be established.
shape_routing_negative.conjunction_pinned: A document is SARIF when it carries version "2.1.0" TOGETHER WITH a runs array -- those two together are the test. The two near-miss fixtures each fail exactly one half, so an implementation checking only version is caught by near-sarif-runs-only.json and one checking only runs is caught by near-sarif-version-only.json. Neither fixture alone pins the conjunction, which is why both are committed.
shape_routing_negative.unknown_shape_halts_by_name: an artifact matching neither SARIF nor a known native shape halts rather than being best-effort parsed, and the halt is asserted to be a raised, named condition -- not a counted rejection, since a rejection would let reconciliation balance over an artifact nobody could read

reconciliation.requirement: AAP 0.6.1 -- asserts raw finding records = dataset rows + rejected records over a fixture containing at least one rejection, that JSON and CSV parsed counts are compared separately, and that an absent artifact records "not applicable -- artifact absent".
reconciliation.identity: raw finding records = dataset rows for that tool + rejected records

at_least_one_rejection_fixture.why_it_matters: an identity asserted over a fixture with zero rejections is satisfied by an implementation that drops rejections entirely

json_and_csv_counted_separately.requirement: the parsed findings.json and parsed findings.csv row counts are compared to the identity SEPARATELY rather than assumed equal
json_and_csv_counted_separately.line_count_prohibition_asserted: equality is asserted by PARSING both files, never by counting lines. The embedded-newline assertion is the falsifiable form of that rule: message fields carry newlines, so a line count over-reports while a parse does not.

absent_artifact_sentinel.never: 0 = 0 + 0, which would assert that a traversal happened and balanced when no traversal was possible
absent_artifact_sentinel.applies_to_this_run: osv-scanner, the one tool of the nine that wrote no artifact

independence_of_the_counting_traversal.requirement: AAP 0.5.4 -- "A count taken from the same traversal that builds the rows satisfies the assertion while testing nothing."
independence_of_the_counting_traversal.asserted_structurally_not_behaviourally: Agreement on a fixture proves nothing, because a delegating implementation agrees on every fixture. So independence is asserted against the import graph and the signatures.

positive_mapping.requirement: AAP 0.9.4 -- an unmodified captured positive fixture per adapter with a field-by-field hand-verified expected result.
positive_mapping.fixture_provenance: Each positive fixture is an unmodified excerpt captured from that tool's own artifact under harness/artifacts/raw/. AAP 0.6.2: "a hand-written fixture tests the adapter against the shape you believed the tool emits rather than the shape it emits."
positive_mapping.expected_results_provenance: hand-verified and asserted field by field, never generated by running the adapter under test
positive_mapping.integrity_asserted: every module's fixture-inventory class asserts every fixture present, parsing, and UNCHANGED BY SHA256, so no assertion can pass over a fixture that silently failed to parse or over an expected file with an empty rows array

sarif.note: three producers, one shared adapter, three captured fixtures

checkov.note: the captured object form plus the multi-framework array form, because both top-level shapes must be handled

non_negative_non_positive_fixtures.halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json: drives the structural halt rather than a row or a rejection
non_negative_non_positive_fixtures.near-sarif-runs-only.json: fails only the version half of the SARIF conjunction
non_negative_non_positive_fixtures.near-sarif-version-only.json: fails only the runs half of the SARIF conjunction
non_negative_non_positive_fixtures.unknown-shape.json: matches neither SARIF nor any known native shape, so it must halt by name
non_negative_non_positive_fixtures.reconcile-mixed.json: the at-least-one-rejection fixture the identity is asserted over

positive_mapping.fixture_accounting: 52 fixtures = 38 negative + 9 positive + 5 above. Every one is claimed by a module's inventory and none sits untested.

per_adapter_assertions.purpose: Named so a reader can SEE coverage rather than infer it. Every method listed executed in the run recorded above and passed; none is a name taken from a docstring without a result behind it.

chained_uriBaseId_walk.why_both: the SARIF specification's own originalUriBaseIds example expresses one base relative to another, so chaining is LEGAL. A guard that refused to chain would pass a cycle test and be wrong; asserting the legal chain resolves is what stops that.

metadata_backed_fallback.conditionality: applies ONLY where the runner metadata supplies an explicit base for that tool, and is otherwise a rejection under unresolvable_path. It is not a catch-all.
metadata_backed_fallback.real_producer_gaps_covered: the two documented producer faults are both exercised -- a uriBaseId emitted with no matching originalUriBaseIds entry (as Opengrep and Semgrep do here, emitting %SRCROOT% with no base map), and ROOTPATH emitted as a bare file:/// inside a git repository

sarif.first_location_counter: the count of records carrying more than one location is asserted to be reported rather than discarded -- the record still counts once
sarif.ascending_rule_is_falsifiable: the CWE assertion is set on inputs where producer order and lexicographic order DISAGREE with numeric order, so an implementation taking the first or the alphabetically smallest fails rather than coincidentally agreeing
sarif.cross_tool_base_refused: AdapterContractTests.test_another_tools_path_base_is_refused -- pass; one tool's recorded base cannot be used to resolve another tool's paths

trivy.why_one_identical_record_under_three_sec: It holds the record's content fixed and varies only its enclosing array. An implementation reading the class off the content produces one class three times and fails; an implementation reading the array produces three.
trivy.the_counterfactual_is_the_point: Trivy 0.74.0 can also emit Licenses and ExperimentalModifiedFindings. A tolerated skip would drop real tool output while reconciliation still balanced, and that arithmetic is MEASURED rather than argued -- which is why the halt is asserted by its exact exception type and the unsupported members are iterated from the constant, so a new member without a case becomes visible.
trivy.unsupported_members_source: the two members Trivy's own report.go declares, asserted against the constant rather than a retyped list

gitleaks.why_the_base_is_the_hard_part: gitleaks dir takes exactly one path and reports relative to the process working directory when handed more, so the base is a property of the INVOCATION rather than of the tool. Both readings are covered, and the base is read from harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json through the real loaders rather than written into a test as a literal -- which is why changing the recorded base is asserted to change every resolved path.
gitleaks.why_that_matters: A sweep that found nothing because it looks for nothing would pass every no-secret assertion. Planting a value and requiring the sweep to FIND it is what establishes the sweep works, over rows and over rejections both.
gitleaks.source_field_confinement: the adapter's row is built from exactly four named keys -- RuleID, Description, File, StartLine -- and the sensitive keys are asserted to be in its never-read set, so Secret and Match are structurally out of reach rather than merely unused
gitleaks.no_severity_vocabulary: gitleaks defines none, so severity_native is absent on every row and severity_norm is Info by the stated no-vocabulary route rather than by an assumed level; a rejected record contributes no severity literal to the tally

checkov.user_worked_example: This is the user's own example, carried in unchanged: file_path such as /folder1/A.tf is relative to the scan root DESPITE its leading slash, and reading that slash as filesystem-absolute produces a long ../ path and a false in_scope: false. The no-parent-segment assertion is the direct guard on that failure.
checkov.why_the_second_assertion_is_load_bearing: "No row corresponds to a passed or skipped check" is vacuously true over a fixture that contains none, so the fixtures are asserted to REALLY carry passed and skipped checks. The shared-identifier case then rules out an implementation that filtered by rule id rather than by bucket.

dependency-check.precedence_is_asserted_level_by_level: each level is asserted with every LOWER level also available, so an implementation that reached for the wrong level would produce a different coordinate rather than coincidentally the right one
dependency-check.selected_entry_recorded: An advisory commonly carries several scores from different sources, so WHICH entry governed is recorded rather than left implicit -- the label where a mapped label exists, or the score with its source and version where none does. The by-version-not-by-magnitude assertion rules out an implementation quietly picking the highest number.
dependency-check.this_is_the_folders_reference_case: for the four-level coordinate precedence and the label-over-score precedence, both of which AAP 0.5.4 fixes once for every dependency-oriented shape

joern.why_both_trees: Every -tests artifact the build produced is in the graph input, so a Joern finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree. The harness collector indexes src/main only, so the adapter extends it -- and the artifact's own file field is an ephemeral /tmp/jimple2cpg-<id>/... path for every finding, which is why resolution goes through the class coordinate instead.
joern.retention_asserted_on_a_named_row: A dropped test-tree row and a retained one are indistinguishable in a row count, so the assertion names the row -- its path, its in_scope value and its presence -- rather than counting.
joern.first_wins_is_not_a_smaller_error: The collector resolves ambiguity first-writer-wins. A first-wins pick is the same error as a wrong path with nothing to show it happened, which is why the ambiguous case is asserted BOTH positively (the expected rejections arrive under the named class) and negatively (no colliding candidate reaches any field of any row).
joern.count_unit_non_vacuous: findings[] is the count unit; the artifact's own queries[] tallies sum to 692 against the fixture's eleven records, so an implementation counting the tallies fails loudly instead of agreeing silently

exit_status.meaning: every test in every module passed

halt_semantics.rule: AAP 0.9.2 -- a failed adapter fixture, rejection or reconciliation test is a condition that STOPS THE RUN.
halt_semantics.never_recorded_as: a soft warning, a known failure, an expected failure, or a skip
halt_semantics.halt_condition_name: a failed adapter fixture, rejection or reconciliation test (AAP 0.9.2)
halt_semantics.no_assertion_was_weakened: skipped, expectedFailures and unexpectedSuccesses are all zero and are reported rather than omitted, so a green result cannot have been obtained by excusing a test. Every one of the 577 methods and 12,955 subTests produced a real verdict.

exit_status.failure_detail: none -- there is no failure or error trace to retain verbatim, because there was none. Had there been, its trace would be retained here as emitted.
exit_status.what_a_failure_here_would_have_meant: The normalizer's correctness claim rests on this suite, so a failure would invalidate oss-scan-results/findings.json, findings.csv and every per-tool number in tool-status.md until diagnosed. The run would report and stop rather than emit a dataset whose adapters had not been shown correct.

coverage_threshold.reason: AAP 0.6.2 sets no coverage threshold. The requirement is positive mapping plus per-condition rejections, and that is what is recorded above. A percentage would be a weaker and less honest claim than the per-fixture enumeration: 100% line coverage over adapters with no negative fixture would still leave every rejection path unexercised.

cross_references.rule: AAP 0.6.4 -- a count appearing in two documents must be one measurement cited twice, never two measurements.

oss-scan-results/tool-status.md.relationship: This record is the SOURCE of the per-tool adapter-fixture result that tool-status.md carries; tool-status.md cites it rather than re-measuring.

values_it_must_agree_with.opengrep: adapter fixture result: pass (shared SARIF adapter, test_sarif_adapter, exit 0)
values_it_must_agree_with.semgrep: adapter fixture result: pass (shared SARIF adapter, test_sarif_adapter, exit 0)
values_it_must_agree_with.datadog-static-analyzer: adapter fixture result: pass (shared SARIF adapter, test_sarif_adapter, exit 0)
values_it_must_agree_with.osv-scanner: adapter fixture result: not applicable -- no artifact, so no adapter, no fixture and no test module; the absent case is covered synthetically by test_reconciliation

oss-scan-results/tool-status.md.nine_tool_inventory: tool-status.md and severity-map.md are the authoritative inventory of all nine tools, because findings.json and findings.csv are row-only and a tool with zero rows is invisible in them by construction (AAP 0.5.4). This record likewise carries all nine, eight through their modules and osv-scanner through its stated conditionality.

harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.jso.relationship: companion record from the same pipeline: it records the normalizer's own run, this one records the tests that establish that normalizer's adapters are correct

agreements.interpreter: /usr/bin/python3 at 3.13.7 in both -- one interpreter, cited twice
agreements.reject_class_vocabulary: the same ten members, both read from normalize.paths rather than retyped

harness/artifacts/logs/normalize-run.jso.ordering: Stage 1 writes runner-metadata.json; the normalizer reads it as input; tool-status.md is rendered afterwards from that metadata joined with the normalization results and with this record. The Markdown is an output of the pipeline, never an input to it.

cross_references.oss-scan-results/run-record.md: owns the index and the manifest; every number here is expected to be citable from it, and this file's own byte size and sha256 belong to that manifest (see own_size_and_digest).
cross_references.oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/README.md: echoes the same commands recorded here; the command form is the one the test modules document, so all three agree by construction rather than by transcription.

own_size_and_digest.location: the per-file byte-size and sha256 manifest that oss-scan-results/run-record.md owns
own_size_and_digest.reason: A file cannot carry its own sha256 without invalidating it. Both values are computed after this file is written and recorded in that manifest, exactly as the sibling records in this directory do.
own_size_and_digest.required_because: .gitignore:31 is artifacts/, so ordinary git collection excludes this tree and the manifest is how it is published (AAP 0.9.4).

what_this_record_deliberately_did_not_do: It did not record a pass for any test that did not execute -- every verdict above came from an invocation whose exit status is recorded beside it.
It did not report a single aggregate pass count in place of the per-fixture enumeration, which is the form that hides whether the rejection paths were ever exercised.
It did not treat the absent OSV module as a gap to paper over, and did not invent a fixture, an expected file or an adapter for an artifact the tool never wrote.
It did not edit, weaken or skip any assertion, and did not touch anything under harness/lib/normalize/ or any fixture -- a defect these tests reveal there is reported, not repaired.
It did not use pytest or any third-party runner, and installed nothing.
It did not silently correct its own two errors -- the class tally and the earlier fixture miscount are recorded with both the wrong and the right value.

It did not judge any finding, compare any tool against another, or characterise what any tool's output shows -- this record is about adapters and their tests, and AAP 0.3.2 forbids cross-tool interpretation of any kind.
It carries no credential and no secret value in any field: the fixtures' synthetic placeholders are self-evidently synthetic and nothing was quoted out of them here.
